startup.name: Tago Health
startup.one_liner: AI agents for healthcare denials and accounts receivable
startup.description: AI agents for the billing back office of US healthcare providers: they investigate denied or underpaid claims, draft and submit appeals, and a voice agent calls payers until payment posts. Works inside practice management systems, clearinghouses and payer portals, with human approval and an audit log. Team of three in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent range, references/yc_acceptance.md). Up because healthcare revenue cycle AI is a current YC theme with clear dollar value per recovered claim. Down because many YC companies already pursue the exact wedge and the team is three people with no stated customers or revenue. Net about 3 percent, conditional on the batch already given.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most likely say that denial management and A/R follow up is a crowded wedge, with multiple recent YC companies and funded rivals doing appeals and payer calls, and that without paying billing teams or a data advantage this is another agent wrapper. Payer integrations and HIPAA make sales slow.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 7.4 months from 2026-04-06 to 2026-11-17 and the number is for a round above about 1M from outside investors closing inside it. Anchor 0.59 B2B ever. The 2022 and later median time to seed is 6 months from batch start, so about 70 percent of eventual seeds come by 7 months at best, but the anchor already mixes the YC deal; 0.44 is 0.75x the anchor, the floor of the calibration rule, and healthcare is slower than the B2B median. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, likely when the company has billing teams piloting but little revenue.
Typical institutional seed in healthcare AI near the 2022 and later median of 4.1M; Cofactor AI raised 4M in a denials focused seed.
Strong seed for a hot agent category with a named design partner and recovered dollars.
Large seed in revenue cycle AI, rare for a three person team.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if billing teams do not pay during the window, if payer portal access proves brittle, or if investors see many similar companies: CombineHealth (Winter 2023) and Substrate (Summer 2024) are active with no priced round found, Ember and Clicks Health reached only a seed, and Egress Health was acquired. Seven months is short for healthcare sales cycles and compliance review.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely outcome is a stall as many similar agent startups compete and billing companies resist new vendors, or an acquisition of the team by an RCM vendor for under 100M, as with Egress Health. The upside requires recovering large dollars across payers with a data advantage; Arintra shows it is possible but over a long time.

killers.risk: Crowded wedge with many YC and funded rivals
killers.evidence: Six or more YC companies target RCM or denials with AI, and funded vendors like Cofactor AI and RapidClaims ship appeals engines.
killers.mitigation: Specialize in a payer or specialty with proprietary denial data.

killers.risk: Slow healthcare sales and security review
killers.evidence: Billing teams require HIPAA reviews and long pilots; Healthcare median months to seed is 19.
killers.mitigation: Sell to outsourced RCM firms that decide fast.

killers.risk: Payer portal and voice call fragility
killers.evidence: Agents that log into portals and call payers break when payers change flows or block bots.
killers.mitigation: Keep humans in the loop and monitor failures.

killers.risk: Team of three and no stated revenue
killers.evidence: The input shows a team of three and lists no customers, revenue or design partners yet.
killers.mitigation: Land a design partner on contingency pricing.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building agents that read denials and draft appeals is feasible with models. The hard parts are reliable integration with practice management systems and payer portals, voice calls to payers, HIPAA security and accuracy. A three person team can ship pilots, but robust coverage across payers takes longer.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbent RCM and EHR vendors have distribution and are shipping agentic denials products; the market search shows several. A rival needs under a year to add appeals drafting.

evidence.claim: Provider cost of fighting denials exceeded 25 billion dollars in 2023 and most denials are overturned on appeal, per trade sources.
Funded startups such as Cofactor AI are raising on this problem.

roadmap.goal: Show recovered dollars for a real billing team.
actions: Run contingency pilots with two billing teams
roadmap.proof: Dollars recovered and win rate on appeals.

actions: Add payer call agent coverage for the top five payers
Get SOC 2 and a trust center to unblock procurement
roadmap.proof: Five paying customers and recovery dollars per month.

pros.evidence: Denied claims and aged A/R are measurable and appeals are often overturned, giving a contingent pricing model.
The product avoids new logins or migrations, lowering adoption friction.

brand.rationale: A short name plus the word Health is clear but generic, like many health startups. Buyers in billing care about results and security, so the name matters little.

narrative.headline: A well aimed but crowded wedge with a three person team: below even odds of a 1M plus round inside seven months and little chance of Series A.
narrative.general_summary: Tago Health sells AI agents that work denials and A/R for US provider billing teams. The pain is large and measurable, but the field has many YC and funded rivals and healthcare sales are slow. The window is 7.4 months from 2026-04-06 to 2026-11-17, which cuts the seed odds to 0.44, the floor of the calibration rule against the 0.59 B2B anchor. Series A in the window is about 3 percent. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2026-04-06 using only the input; no customers or revenue stated.
Seed means above about 1M from outside investors inside the 7.4 month window.
Analog comps from the same period were not used for outcomes.
